newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar Occidental to raise oil production.
newsitem.headline: Qatar Occidental to raise oil production.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum of Qatar said on Tuesday it had devised a five-year plan to increase oil production at an offshore field off Qatar's eastern coast to 150,000 barrels a day (bpd).
The field -- the Idd El Shargi North Dome (ISND) -- currently produces at an average rate of 80,000 bpd.

"To optimize the recoverable oil reserves from the ISND reservoirs, Oxy, in consultation with Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC), have devised an ambitious development plan requiring 80 wells...to increase the production to a peak of 150,000 bpd," said Occidental Petroleum of Qatar vice-president and general manager, Charles DesBrisay.

Occidental Petroleum of Qatar is a part of the U.S. Occidental Petroleum Ltd, or Oxy. It took over the field as operator in 1995 under a 25-year production-sharing agreement with the state's QGPC when the field's production had dropped to less than 20,000 bpd.
Oxy launched a $750 million development programme to halt the decline and boost output.

"Since inception Oxy, in partnership with QGPC, has successfully progressed an ambitious reservoir development and drilling programme to more than double the ISND field production to a current average rate of 80,000 bpd," DesBrisay said.

Oxy's plan is part of a vigorous QGPC drive to raise the country's oil production to more than 700,000 bpd by 2000. So far the state has boosted its capacity to 550,000 bpd by opening new fields and introducing new production technology.

Qatar is a member of the 11-member Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries allowed to produce 378,000 b/d under an Opec ceiling. But the country is known to be producing over 520,000 b/d currently according to independent estimates.
